rationale: An exported input DTO shape for creating annotations, with fields elementId, author, content and tags. It is a record/DTO type definition, so it maps to a data-model object schema. It has no callers and sits as a minor part of the annotation store API.

Nested recursive helper inside computeDirectoryHashes that walks a directory and hashes files. It is an implementation detail of a hashing utility, not an architectural element. It reads the filesystem directly. The console.error call is incidental error reporting, not telemetry.

Private markdown formatting helper that appends a table of matched entries to a lines buffer. It is called only by formatVerifyMarkdown. As a pure formatting detail, it is not an architecturally meaningful element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

CLI 'add' command module. It validates the layer and type, generates IDs, loads the model, and adds an element via the mutation handler, which persists to disk. It sets span attributes and drives CLI output and errors. This is a user-facing command entry point, modeled as an application function within the CLI component.

Small internal helper interface pairing an HTTP method with endpoint data inside the OpenAPI exporter. It has no callers and is a structural implementation detail of the export logic, not an architecturally meaningful element.

Graph algorithm method in the relationship audit connectivity analyzer. It computes connected components via BFS and caches them in memory. It is internal analysis behaviour used by the audit orchestrator, so it is a notable application function rather than a service. No cross-cutting concerns are implemented; the cache is in-memory only.

Orchestrates the CLI upgrade workflow: displays the plan, handles dry-run, prompts for confirmation, then executes spec, model and integration upgrades in order. It is an ordered application process. It renders CLI output and prompts directly and sets span attributes itself. Persistence and integrations are delegated to callees.

An exported TypeScript interface defining the data shape used to generate a model README report: project metadata, counts and layer summaries. It is a report-specific DTO consumed internally by the report generator, not a canonical domain schema. It is a minor application data object.

An exported TypeScript interface that defines the shape of a validation issue (layer, message, severity, category, fix suggestion) shared across validators. It is a structured application data object rather than a canonical domain schema. It is a notable internal contract within the validation module, but not a core architectural element.

A static method that computes model statistics (element counts, relationship predicates, orphan detection) over an in-memory model. It is shared by CLI commands, the MCP tool and the formatter outputs. It is notable internal behaviour, but it does no I/O or rendering itself.

A report-generation class that produces model README markdown from ModelReadmeData. It is a notable internal unit used by ModelReportOrchestrator. It only builds strings and does no file writing, so no persistence concern applies. It is not UI rendering itself.

An inline arrow function in a color map that wraps a string in red ANSI styling for the 'critical' strength label. It is a trivial formatting helper with no callers or callees, an implementation detail below architectural modelling level.

A plain options interface describing the CLI export command's parameters: format, output path, layers, model and includeSources. It is a minor internal data shape consumed only by the export command. Best modelled as an application data object of low significance. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Core repair logic that recovers collided attribute values by scanning staged changesets from storage, newest first. It is internal behaviour invoked by the repair command, so an application function of notable but not central significance. It reads persisted changesets via storage.list, which counts as data persistence.

Private string-sanitizing helper that replaces path traversal and illegal filename characters before its callers write files. It is a trivial implementation detail with no I/O of its own, so it is not an architectural element.

A specific CLI error subclass with a preset message and suggestion strings. This is boilerplate error typing below the level an architecture model would record. It is a minor unit with no callers in the graph.

A WebSocket JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher that exposes the chat protocol (chat.status, chat.send, chat.cancel) to browser clients. It validates params, launches or kills coding-agent subprocesses, and returns protocol errors. It is a non-HTTP access point to the chat service, so it is modelled as an application interface rather than an OpenAPI operation.

Validator component that composes the base validator with cross-model reference resolution. It loads farm manifests and external models from disk and validates qualified references across models. It is invoked by the validate command, making it a significant validation component of the CLI.

Module defining SemanticValidator, one of the model validation pipeline's validators. It checks relationship predicates against the generated spec index and flags APM elements with inferred provenance. It is a notable internal unit of the validation subsystem. It does no I/O, and it does no telemetry work itself: it only inspects model data.

A small exported TypeScript interface describing the result of a changeset-import compatibility check: snapshot match, missing elements, warnings and affected layers. It is a passive data shape used by the changeset exporter, so it fits application dataobject. It has no callers and is a minor internal unit.

A small TypeScript interface describing the shape of the analyzer registry manifest: a spec version plus a list of analyzer metadata. It is a data shape definition, so it maps to an object schema. It is minor and used only internally by the registry module, with no callers.

A data-shaping helper that normalizes a raw CBM graph node into a route record with defaults. It is called only by verify() and was extracted for testability. It is pure transformation logic with no I/O, below the level an architecture model would record.

Utility module providing kebab-case conversion, element ID formatting and UUID generation. It encodes a naming convention ({layer}.{type}.{name}), but it is pure string helper code with no architectural role of its own, so it would not be recorded as a model element.

Exported class that loads and strictly validates the .dr-verify-ignore.yaml rules file from disk for the verify analyzer. It is a notable internal unit of the verification subsystem that reads a configuration file, which counts as data persistence. It is not a standalone service or system boundary.

This is a CRUD method on the in-memory GraphModel. It removes an edge and keeps the source, destination and predicate indices consistent. It is an ordinary internal unit of the core graph component, below service level, with no storage, I/O or cross-cutting concerns.

A TypeScript interface describing the shape of a layer distribution JSON file that contains relationship schema definitions. It is a data shape (object schema) used internally by the relationship schema validator. It is not exported beyond this file's use and has no callers, so it is a minor internal type.

Private helper that formats a markdown table section of a README report. It is pure string formatting called only by generate(). It is an implementation detail with no architectural standing of its own, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

This is the main entry method of StatsCollector. It runs the layer, relationship, validation, orphan and completeness sub-collections and aggregates them into a ModelStats object for reporting. It is internal application behaviour over in-memory model data: it does no direct I/O and is not telemetry, so no cross-cutting concerns apply.

Component of the audit pipeline that formats audit results as JSON, Markdown or text and writes report files to disk. It is a notable internal unit used by PipelineOrchestrator, and it persists its output to the filesystem. It is not telemetry and not an interactive UI.

Core module providing the DependencyTracker class, which uses graph algorithms over the reference registry to trace dependencies and assess impact between model elements. This is a significant analysis component of the CLI core. It does no I/O, auth, or rendering itself.

Abstract base class defining the contract for chat CLI clients (availability check, sendMessage, session handling). It is a central abstraction for pluggable coding-agent integrations. Concrete subclasses perform the external calls; this base itself only manages in-memory session state, so it implements no cross-cutting concern directly.

A small exported TypeScript interface that describes the validation summary within the stats collector's output (validity flag, timestamp, error and warning counts). It is a passive data shape used only inside the stats module, so it is a minor application dataobject.

CLI command module registering the 'dr claude' subcommand group (install/upgrade/remove/status/list). It is a user-facing CLI access point to the Claude integration manager, and it defines the CLI options and help text. File I/O is delegated to ClaudeIntegrationManager.

This is a no-op arrow-function property on a stub span object used when telemetry is disabled. It does no telemetry work itself and is trivial scaffolding with no callers, so it is not an architecturally meaningful element.

Private helper that serializes an inter-layer validation result to a JSON file in the output directory. It is a persistence implementation detail of the AIEvaluator rather than an architecturally meaningful element in its own right. It does write to disk, so data_persistence applies.

Trivial formatting helper that wraps a string in ANSI blue when colors are enabled. It is an implementation detail of CLI output styling with no callers, so it is not an architecturally meaningful element on its own.

Trivial getter that delegates to the loader's isLoaded check. It reports initialization state of SpecDataService and has no callers. It is an implementation detail, not an architectural element on its own.

ApiKeyManager generates, stores, loads, rotates and validates (constant-time) API keys used to authenticate MCP server clients. It persists keys and config to disk with restricted permissions. It is the credential-management mechanism for the MCP server, so it is security-layer authentication and architecturally significant.

A CLI-wide error handling module that defines the error taxonomy, exit-code categories and formatted terminal error output. It is a cross-cutting internal utility that maintainers would name, but it is not a service or boundary. It renders CLI output, so user_interface is true.

CLI command module for 'dr reports regenerate'. It registers the subcommand and deletes and reads the reports directory on disk, which counts as persistence. It also prints CLI output. Report generation itself is delegated to the orchestrator. This is a notable command component rather than a core boundary.

CLI command module implementing element search across the model. It loads the model from disk, filters elements by layer, type and source file, renders table or JSON output, and sets span attributes. As a user-facing CLI command it is a notable application function, not a core abstraction.

The module defines shared Zod input field schemas, with validation constraints, for the annotation_* MCP tools. These are fragments of the tool contract surface, closest to inline API schemas. They are small reusable field definitions that matter mainly to the annotation tool modules, so significance is low.

The module manages a shared golden-copy test model that is cloned via filesystem copy to speed up test initialization. That makes it test fixture infrastructure, despite its src/core location. It writes to temp directories, so it touches persistence. No listed testing element type fits a fixture cache, hence null. It is a notable support unit rather than a core element.

CLI command module registering ten analyzer subcommands (discover, status, index, query, verify). It is a user-facing entry point to the analyzer subsystem: it renders CLI output and prompts, persists session state to disk, and drives external analyzer backends. Best modelled as an application interface.

Small nested helper inside deleteCommand that formats and prints success and cascade-confirmation messages to the CLI. It is pure output formatting with no architectural role of its own, so it is an implementation detail that only drives user-facing CLI output.

The module formats verification reports as text (ANSI-coloured), JSON, or markdown for CLI output. It is a notable internal output-formatting unit within the export subsystem and drives user-facing CLI presentation. It does not persist data or integrate with external systems, so it is modelled as an application function of moderate significance.

A one-line convenience wrapper on SpecDataLoader that delegates to findRelationshipTypes with a destination filter. It is a trivial query helper with no independent architectural role. It operates on in-memory spec data and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Pure in-memory analysis class that compares two audit reports across coverage, gaps, duplicates, balance and connectivity. It is used by the audit-diff command and the pipeline orchestrator, making it a notable component of the audit subsystem. It does no I/O or rendering.

A trivial pure helper that downgrades a 'high' confidence value to 'medium' for heuristic analyzer results. It has no architectural role of its own and is an implementation detail used by CbmAnalyzer transforms.

Application component orchestrating AI-based evaluation of layer node schemas. It composes a prompt template, an AI runner and a parser, then aggregates scores. It writes progress messages to stderr (CLI output). The external Claude call is delegated to AuditAIRunner, so external integration is not marked. It is a notable unit within the audit subsystem.

A validator component that checks architecture models for semantic rules: relationship predicates must be defined in the spec, and it warns when all APM elements are inferred. It is one sub-validator composed by the main Validator, so it is a notable internal component. It inspects APM model data but does not emit telemetry itself.

A small utility module holding in-memory global CLI option state (verbose/debug/json flags) plus conditional console logging helpers. It is a minor internal cross-cutting utility, not a service or component. The logVerbose and logDebug helpers do the logging work themselves, so observability applies.

Internal behaviour of the audit RelationshipGraph: it builds an in-memory graph of spec node types and relationships for connectivity analysis. This is a notable internal unit, not a service boundary. The console.error warnings are incidental diagnostics rather than telemetry. It does no persistent I/O.

Small query method on SpecDataService that derives the unique relationship predicates valid between two spec node types using in-memory loader data. It is internal application behaviour with no callers, so it has minor significance and touches no cross-cutting concern.

A simple exported interface holding in-memory performance counters (init and clone counts and timings) for the golden-copy model cache. It is a minor data shape used only alongside the cache. It does not emit telemetry itself, so observability is false. It is modelled as an application data object of low significance.

Public entry method of the layer report generator that orchestrates the section builders into a complete markdown report. It is internal application behaviour invoked by the report orchestrator. It returns a string rather than writing files or rendering UI, so no cross-cutting concerns apply. Notable within the reports module.

Small helper that writes MCP tool failures to stderr for operator visibility. It does logging work, so observability applies, but it is a trivial internal utility with a single caller (runTool). It is not a meaningful telemetry element worth modelling in the APM layer.

Exported interface defining a single step in the mutation handler pipeline: an execute function, a stageable flag and a description. It is a notable internal contract within the mutation-handling component. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of a relationship type entry in the relationship catalog (predicate, inverse, category, semantics, applicable layers). It is a domain record/schema type rather than behaviour, so it fits data-model objectschema. It is notable within the catalog module but not a core boundary.

Analysis class within the relationship audit subsystem that groups relationship specs by endpoints and flags semantic duplicates by predicate category or inverse. It is used by AuditOrchestrator, making it a notable internal component. The console.warn debug output is incidental and does not amount to an observability concern.

Internal parser that extracts and validates node evaluation JSON from Claude responses for the AI audit evaluator. It is a notable internal unit of the audit pipeline but is not a service boundary. It does not call the external AI itself, so no external_integration concern applies.

Recursively hashes files in a directory to support integration install and update detection. It is an internal utility used by BaseIntegrationManager, so it is notable rather than core. It reads files from disk, which counts as data persistence. Its console.error call is incidental and does not count as observability.

StagingAreaManager method that captures a model hash snapshot for drift detection and persists it on the changeset via storage. It is internal application behavior supporting changeset staging, and a maintainer would name it when explaining drift detection. It persists data by saving the changeset.

Module of type definitions for the relationship audit system (CoverageMetrics, DuplicateCandidate, GapCandidate, BalanceAssessment). It defines the domain record shapes used by audit analysis, so it fits the data model as object schemas. It is a notable shared contract for the audit subsystem but holds no behaviour beyond a small validator.

A small path-resolution helper that joins the documentation-robotics directory with 'model' and checks that the path exists. It is a utility used by several commands, not an architecturally meaningful element. The filesystem existence check is incidental and delegated to fileExists, so the symbol does no persistence work itself.

A small internal data shape for conformance-check results within the conformance command, holding a severity and a message. It is a minor DTO-like application data object with no callers and no cross-cutting behaviour.

Trivial string formatting helper that converts camelCase type names into spaced, capitalized text for markdown link labels. It is called only by a sibling helper, so it is an implementation detail with no architectural role.

A pluggable Exporter implementation that serializes the architecture model to GraphML. It is one of several format exporters used by the export command and MCP tool. It emits telemetry spans directly. It returns a string rather than writing files, so it has no persistence concern.

Private helper that filters a layer's node type names by substring pattern. It is a trivial in-memory filter with no architectural role beyond supporting GapAnalyzer.analyzeLayerWithStatus, so it is an implementation detail.

A small internal type in the composed reference validator. It holds a resolved external model's name and its element IDs for cross-model reference lookup. It has no callers and is a local implementation detail, not a canonical schema, so it carries no architectural weight.

Manifest is a core domain data object holding project metadata, changeset history and external model declarations, with JSON (de)serialization and legacy migration. Model.init and Model.load depend on it and it has many callers, so it is architecturally significant. It does not itself perform any file I/O.

A small exported interface with two optional fields (handler, path) describing an ignore pattern for the verify analyzer. It is a minor internal configuration shape with no callers recorded. Too fine-grained to model as a data-model entity, so it is classed as none with low significance.

Private method that builds the VerifyReport object from match buckets, a summary and changeset context. It is internal report-assembly logic inside VerifyEngine with a single caller (computeReport). It performs no I/O and no cross-cutting work, so it is a minor internal application function.

A bundled JSON Schema document that defines the node schemas for the Application layer in the Documentation Robotics spec. It is a canonical schema contract consumed for validating model elements. That makes it a significant data-model artifact, specifically a root JSON Schema collection, rather than executable application code.

This is a no-op stub property inside a fake span object, used when telemetry is disabled. It is a trivial arrow function that returns noopSpan and records nothing. It is an implementation detail of the telemetry module, not an architectural element, so it does not itself implement observability.

The module defines the Exporter contract, export options and format metadata that all format-specific exporters implement. It acts as an internal application interface for the export subsystem. It also holds shared constants and an XML escape helper. As a types module it is notable but not core, so significance is 2.

A formatting function that renders a NodeAuditReport as a Markdown string. It is a format-specific implementation detail dispatched by formatNodeAuditReport. It does no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern, so it is not recorded as an architecture element on its own.

Utility module of small helpers for call graph analysis: depth clamping, shaping raw response nodes into CallGraphNode, and determining edge types. These are pure transformation helpers with no callers recorded and no architectural boundary, so it is not an element a model would record. The console.warn is incidental, not an observability concern.

CopilotClient is an adapter component that integrates with the external GitHub Copilot CLI by spawning a subprocess. It extends BaseChatClient, manages chat sessions, and emits telemetry spans directly. It is one of several pluggable chat clients and serves as an integration point, so it is architecturally significant.

Orchestrator module that loads the project model from disk and sequences the coverage, gap, duplicate, balance and connectivity analyzers into an AuditReport. It is a key coordinating unit of the audit subsystem, best modelled as an application process. It reads persisted model files through Model.load.

Reads and validates the persisted analyzer session state from session.json on disk, returning null when the file is missing. It is an exported persistence function used by the analyzer commands, so it counts as a notable internal application function rather than a dedicated data-store element.

A CLI subcommand handler that reverts a staged changeset. It does this by delegating to StagingAreaManager, which performs the persistence. The function itself sets span attributes and status, so observability is true. It also renders CLI output in colored text or JSON, so user_interface is true. It is a notable unit within the changeset command group.

Module housing RelationshipValidator, a core validation component that loads bundled relationship schemas from disk and enforces schema compliance, predicates and cardinality on model relationships. It reads manifest and layer files from disk and wraps validation in telemetry spans, making it an architecturally significant application component.

A pluggable Exporter implementation that converts the data-model layer of the architecture graph into a JSON Schema document. It is used by the CLI export command and the MCP export tool, which makes it a replaceable application component. It emits telemetry spans directly. It returns a string and does no file I/O itself.

Exported TypeScript interface defining a record shape for analyzer output: a route entry found only in the graph, carrying an id, HTTP method/path and source location. It is a plain DTO type with no behaviour and no callers, so it ranks as a minor data-model object schema.

Core behaviour of the JSON Schema exporter. It transforms data-model graph nodes and edges into a JSON Schema document string. This is internal application functionality behind an export feature, not a schema definition itself. It records its own telemetry span attributes, so observability is true. It does no file I/O, returning a string instead.

Simple in-memory aggregation method on RelationshipRegistry that computes counts of relationships, predicates, layers and types. It has no callers and does no I/O, so it is an implementation detail of the registry component rather than an architectural element of its own.

Small internal interface pairing an MCP server instance with its HTTP transport per session. It is an in-memory record used inside the HTTP transport module, with no callers elsewhere. It is a minor application data object, not a persisted entity, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Module defining the data shapes for integration management: component config, the version-file YAML schema with a validator, file-change records and obsolete-file records. These are domain type and schema definitions, so they belong in the data model. The module defines but does not itself perform file I/O, so no concerns apply.

The Exporter interface is the contract that all export-format plugins implement. It defines a name, the layers each exporter supports, and an async export of a Model. That makes it a central extension point of the export subsystem, best modelled as an application interface. It performs no I/O itself.

Bundled JSON configuration for the codebase-memory-mcp analyzer. It declares the external MCP server's required and optional tool contract, its binary names, and how its graph node labels map to DR layers and element types. This makes it a significant configuration artifact that defines an external integration point.

Module defines the abstract chat client contract (BaseChatClient plus message, session and options types) that Claude Code and Copilot CLI adapters implement. It is a key integration abstraction point. The module itself declares the interface but does not spawn processes or call external systems.

An options/configuration interface for the base chat client that wraps coding agents (Claude, Copilot). It is a passive data structure shaping how chat invocations behave and is part of the client contract. It is notable within the module, but it only declares fields and implements no concern itself.

Private helper inside GapAnalyzer that maps a layer ID and type name to a priority label using simple string checks. It is a small heuristic used by one caller, an implementation detail below the level of an architectural element, and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Core verification engine comparing code-graph discovered routes against the DR model's API layer, producing a matched/in_graph_only/in_model_only/ignored report. It loads the model and ignore rules from disk. It is a notable analyzer component invoked by CbmAnalyzer, so it is modelled as an application component of architectural significance.

Core module centralizing all element add/update/delete mutations across the staging area and the base model, and handling persistence atomically. It is an architecturally significant application component. It writes durable model and changeset state and emits telemetry logs directly via emitLog.

Core engine that computes virtual model projections by applying staged changesets to the base model, with a TTL cache. It is used by the staging manager, the changeset validator and Model, which makes it a significant application component. It loads changesets from disk-backed staged storage.

A private helper inside MarkdownGenerator that builds a Mermaid graph string from a layer's nodes and intra-layer edges. It is internal export formatting logic called only by generateLayerDiagram. It is a minor internal function, does no I/O, and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Core repair function that applies recovered attribute values to model elements in memory, called by the repair command. It is internal application behaviour, an applicationfunction. It mutates in-memory layers without saving, so no persistence concern applies. It is a notable unit within the collision-repair module.

A small exported TypeScript interface describing a relationship record inside the data-model analyzer's results. It is an internal analysis DTO rather than a canonical domain schema, so it is modelled as an application data object of minor significance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Central coordinator for the relationship audit subsystem. It composes the coverage, duplicate, gap, balance and connectivity analyzers over the relationship catalog and graph. PipelineOrchestrator consumes it, making it an architecturally significant application component. Its catalog loading is delegated, and its logging is incidental rather than telemetry.

Core class that hashes in-memory model state into SHA-256 snapshots and detects drift. The staging area and changeset exporter depend on it. It is internal application logic with no I/O of its own, making it a notable supporting component rather than a system boundary.

A small options interface for a CLI docs-generation command, holding only optional output and layer fields. It is a boilerplate parameter shape with no callers or behaviour, so it is too minor to record as an architecture element.

MCP tool handler exposing the model_add operation to external MCP clients. It validates the layer, type and attributes, builds an Element and persists it through MutationHandler (staged or committed). It is an exposed application service at an MCP boundary, not an HTTP route, so it belongs in the application layer.

Class that generates per-layer markdown reports, including diagrams, tables and element references. It is used by ModelReportOrchestrator. It is a notable internal report-generation component. It only builds strings and does no file writes, so no cross-cutting concerns apply; the markdown output is a document artifact rather than an interactive UI.

ExportManager is the central registry and dispatcher for pluggable model exporters. It is used by both the CLI export command and the MCP export tool, which makes it a significant application component. It performs no I/O or persistence itself; it only validates layer support and delegates the export to registered exporters.

An exported TypeScript interface that defines the shape of a source-reference record: provenance, optional locations and repository context. It is a domain type shared across the model, so it fits the data-model layer as an object schema. It is notable but not a central architectural element.

A simple custom Error subclass that signals an abort after repeated AI evaluation failures. It carries only a message and a cause, has no behaviour of its own, and is used by a single caller, so it is not modelled as an architectural element.

A small internal stats shape that the validation formatter uses to summarise element and relationship counts for output. It is a local helper type with no callers outside its file, so it is too minor to model as an architecture element.

A small interface holding cache hit, miss and invalidation counters, used to monitor the virtual projection cache. It is a metrics shape, so it maps loosely to apm metricinstrument and implements observability. Significance is low because it is an internal type with no callers outside its file.

A private formatting helper inside MarkdownGenerator. It counts graph nodes and edges and renders a markdown statistics table string. This is an implementation detail of the export component, not an architectural element. It does no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern.

The module contains only type definitions, which describe the shape of specification metadata: layers, node types, relationships, predicates and statistics. These are domain data shapes consumed by the SpecDataLoader, so they fit the data-model layer as object schemas. They matter internally to the loader but are not a service or boundary.

ModelDiff is an exported TypeScript interface that describes the computed difference between a base model and a virtual projection: additions, modifications and deletions per element. It is an internal data structure processed by the projection component, so it fits an application dataobject rather than a canonical schema. It is notable within the module but not core.

A custom OpenTelemetry SpanExporter that converts spans to OTLP JSON and POSTs them via fetch to a collector endpoint with a timeout. It is the telemetry export integration point, wrapped by ResilientOTLPExporter, and fits the APM exporter configuration concept.

Analysis class that classifies model relationships against the relationship catalog, computing category breakdowns and transitivity analysis. It is a notable internal analysis component used for reporting. It performs no direct I/O itself, since catalog loading is delegated, and its only caller is its unit test.

Core component handling changeset export/import across YAML, JSON and patch formats, plus compatibility validation against the current model. It reads and writes files and loads staged changesets from storage. It is used by the CLI export and import commands, making it a significant application component.

MCP tool handler exposing annotation update functionality to external MCP clients. It validates its input and delegates persistence to AnnotationStore, so it does not write storage itself. It is one of several similar tool handlers, which puts it at notable rather than core significance. It serves an external protocol.

Private method of SpecDataLoader that reads bundled per-layer JSON files listed in the manifest and returns sorted layer specs. It is an internal loading step that only its class cares about. It reads durable files from disk, so data_persistence is true.

An exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of a constraint-analysis result record (entity id, constraint kind, description, validity). It is a DTO shape used only inside the data-model analyzer module, with no callers or behaviour, so its significance is minor.

Bundled JSON Schema (draft-07) document defining the node schemas for the security layer of the Documentation Robotics spec. It is a canonical data contract used to validate model elements, not runtime security logic, so it belongs in data-model as a jsonschema and implements no cross-cutting concerns itself.

Internal step of the upgrade command that installs the spec reference. It wraps the work in a telemetry span and prints CLI status output. The actual file writes are delegated to installSpecReference, so data_persistence is false. It is a notable unit within the upgrade command module.

Validates a source/predicate/destination relationship triple against the relationship catalog and builds suggestion messages when it fails. This is internal validation behaviour used by the relationship add command, so it is an application function. A maintainer would name it when explaining the module, but it is not a core boundary.

The module defines the ReportGenerator class, which renders audit results as JSON, markdown or text and writes the report files to disk. It is a notable internal component of the audit subsystem rather than a system boundary. Persisting the report files is its only cross-cutting concern.

A trivial one-line lookup on the registry's in-memory predicate map, with no callers. It is an implementation detail of RelationshipRegistry rather than an element an architecture model would record on its own.

An abstract base class for the integration managers (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) that install integration files, track versions and hashes in YAML version files, and resolve source and target directories. It is a central reusable component for the integrations subsystem, and it reads and writes files on disk.

A bundled JSON Schema document that defines node schemas for the Product layer's element types (capability, feature, milestone, and so on). It is a canonical, shared schema contract used to validate architecture model elements. That makes it an architecturally significant data-model artifact, not product-layer content itself.

Module providing the DataModelAnalyzer class and its result interfaces, which analyse the architecture model's data-model layer (entities, constraints, coverage, quality). This is application analysis logic over an in-memory model, not a data-model definition itself. It is a notable internal component of the reporting and analysis subsystem.

Exported TypeScript interface describing the shape of complexity metrics computed by the data-model analyzer. It is a passive data structure internal to the analysis module, with no callers recorded. That makes it a minor application data object rather than a canonical domain schema, and it implements no cross-cutting concerns.

An analysis component within the relationship audit subsystem. It computes per-layer relationship coverage metrics (isolation, predicate utilization, density, standard alignment) and is used by AuditOrchestrator. It is a notable internal unit rather than a system boundary. It writes partial-failure warnings to the console as CLI output.

A trivial in-memory mutator that resets the ambiguities array on FarmSyncState. It has no callers or callees and does no persistence itself. This is an implementation detail of the parent state class, not an architectural element on its own.

Central component that registers and applies versioned model migrations for the upgrade command. It is model-schema migration logic inside the application, not a database migration table. Later migrations likely modify model files on disk, so it counts as data persistence. It is a significant internal component.

A trivial one-line delegating accessor on SpecDataService that forwards a lookup to SpecDataLoader.getNodeType. It has no callers and no logic of its own. It is an implementation detail of the service rather than a modelled architectural element.

A trivial accessor that returns the build-injected CLI version constant and falls back to dev version resolution. It is used in several places but is a utility, not an architectural element. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Exporter plugin implementing the Exporter interface. It converts the model's api layer into an OpenAPI 3.0 spec and is used by the CLI export command and the MCP export tool. It is an application component, not an API route itself. It starts telemetry spans directly, so observability is true.

CLI entry-point command orchestrating an interactive AI chat session: loads the model, detects external AI chat CLIs, prompts for a client selection, writes session logs to disk, and emits telemetry spans. This is an application-level process at the system boundary with an external agent integration.

Central mutation orchestrator shared by CLI commands and MCP tools. It routes add/update/delete either through a staging changeset or into the persisted base model, capturing before/after states. It does the persistence work itself (_persistChanges, staging), which makes it an architecturally significant application component.

Small utility module of string-formatting helpers for markdown link text, such as title-casing node type names and avoiding markdownlint MD059 prohibited phrases. It has no callers or callees. This is a trivial formatting detail with no architectural role.

A private method of RelationshipValidator that enforces relationship cardinality rules (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one) by counting matching relationships and returning violations. It is a notable piece of internal validation behaviour, invoked only by validateRelationship, and touches no storage, I/O, telemetry, or UI itself.

An exported result DTO for the farm sync engine, describing sync outcome, file diffs, element mappings and the staged changeset. It is a passive data structure for internal processing, so it maps to application dataobject. It is notable within the sync module but is not itself a service or contract.

A trivial re-export module wrapping a synchronous version getter in an async function for analyzer compatibility. It has no architectural behaviour of its own and is pure boilerplate below modelling granularity.

Module providing PromptTemplates that build LLM prompt strings for the AI-assisted relationship audit. It is a notable internal unit of the audit subsystem but performs no I/O itself; it only generates text consumed by the AI evaluator, making it an internal application function rather than an integration point.

A private validation helper inside NodeResponseParser. It checks the shape of one AI evaluation item and clamps its scores. It is an internal parsing step that matters only to its parser class, so it is minor application logic rather than a standalone architectural element.

CLI module that registers an 'element' subcommand group (add/list/show/delete/update) with Commander, delegating to existing command handlers. It defines part of the CLI's user-facing interface but is an alternative wiring layer with no logic of its own, so it is moderately significant.

Formatting method that builds a colored CLI error message string from the error's context and suggestions. It is a presentation helper on an error class, with no architectural standing of its own. It does produce CLI-facing output, so user_interface is true.

A simple in-memory implementation of the ProgressTracker interface, used by AIEvaluator to track completed evaluation items. It is a minor internal unit with no persistence, being in-memory only, and it does no telemetry or logging. It matters only to the evaluator module.

Core CLI command handler that resolves source and target elements, validates the relationship against the schema and catalog, guards against duplicates, then stages it or persists it via saveRelationships/saveManifest. It is a central application behavior of the relationship command, not an HTTP API. Telemetry is emitted only through a call to emitLog.

A simple result DTO for the import operation, reporting success, node and edge counts, and errors. It is internal application data, not a canonical domain schema, so it maps to an application dataobject. No callers are recorded, so its significance is minor.

An inline arrow function passed as a config option that returns randomUUID() for MCP transport session IDs. It is a trivial one-line callback with no callers and no logic of its own, so it is an implementation detail rather than a modelled element.

An exported TypeScript interface that defines the shape of audit snapshot metadata records (id, timestamp, model info, layers, file path). It is a domain record type, so it maps to an object schema. It is notable within the audit snapshot storage module but is a passive type that performs no persistence work itself.

Module implementing the CodingAgent adapter for the Claude Code CLI: spawns the external `claude` subprocess, streams stdin/stdout and parses JSON events. It is a pluggable integration component and a significant integration point with an external tool.

Trivial accessor on ExportManager that returns the registered export-format metadata sorted by name. It is an implementation detail of the registry rather than a standalone architectural element, and it has no callers. It implements no cross-cutting concern.

A trivial helper that reads the spec/VERSION file and trims its contents. It is an implementation detail of NodeSchemaLoader with no callers, so it is not architecturally meaningful. It does read from disk, which counts as data persistence.

A static configuration module holding per-layer relationship templates (expected source/destination/predicate patterns) that the audit gap analysis uses for standards alignment. It is a notable internal reference dataset, not behaviour. It is best modelled as an application data object of moderate significance, with no cross-cutting concerns.

A pluggable importer implementing the Importer interface. It parses OpenAPI specs and populates the architecture model graph with nodes and edges. It is registered by ImportManager as a format-specific component. It emits telemetry spans directly. It only mutates the in-memory model, so it does not persist data itself.

Enforces the read-safe permission invariants for coding agents: an allowlist of tools, no write access, and restricted Bash scope. This is access-control policy logic governing what an agent may do, so it belongs in the security layer as a significant authorization policy.

An orchestrator step that delegates duplicate detection to DuplicateDetector, optionally scoped to a single layer. It is a thin internal application function called only by runAudit. It does not itself persist data, call external systems, or emit telemetry; its log call is a verbose-output helper.

An exported type definition describing the shape of a backup manifest: a list of backed-up files plus a creation timestamp. It is a domain record schema, so it maps to a data-model object schema. The type only defines structure and performs no I/O itself, so no concerns apply.

Module implementing a custom OTLP span exporter that POSTs traces via fetch to a collector endpoint. It is telemetry export infrastructure, which makes it an APM exporter element. It integrates with an external OTLP collector over HTTP and is a significant integration point for observability.

PipelineOrchestrator coordinates a multi-step audit pipeline: a before audit, AI evaluation, an after audit, then differential reports. It is an ordered application process composing several components. It writes directories and snapshots to disk and prints CLI progress. AI/Claude calls are delegated to AIEvaluator, so external integration is not marked here.

A trivial one-line function that clears the module-level singleton chat logger instance. Its only caller is a unit test, so it is test-support scaffolding rather than an architectural element. It performs no logging work itself.

PromptTemplates builds LLM prompt strings for the AI relationship audit evaluator, covering element evaluation, layer review and inter-layer gap prompts. It is pure string construction used by AIEvaluator and makes no external calls itself. It is a notable internal unit of the audit AI subsystem, not a service boundary.

Core mutation behaviour of MutationHandler: it deletes an element either by staging the deletion in the active changeset or by removing it from the model layer and its relationships, then persisting. This is a notable internal application function. It writes durable state through staging and _persistChanges.

A small lookup helper in the relationship CLI command module. It queries the relationship catalog for the cardinality and strength constraints of a source/predicate/destination triple. This is internal behaviour supporting validation, of minor significance, and it performs no I/O or other cross-cutting work itself.

A pure string-formatting helper that escapes Markdown special characters. It is widely reused by the export formatters, but it is a trivial utility with no architectural role, so it sits below the level the model would record.

Trivial helper that returns the root path, or an empty string, as a cache key for the loadModel and reloadModel helpers. It holds no architectural responsibility, performs no I/O and is an implementation detail.

Express middleware factory that extracts a Bearer token from the Authorization header, validates it through ApiKeyManager, and rejects requests with a 401. It is the authentication gate protecting the MCP HTTP transport, a system boundary, so it counts as architecturally significant security logic.

A BFS traversal over the in-memory graph model. It is a notable internal capability of the core GraphModel component, exposed upward through Model.traverse, but it is an algorithmic method rather than a service or boundary. It performs no I/O and touches no cross-cutting concern.

A small error subclass of CLIError that formats a not-found message with CLI suggestions. It has no callers and is error-handling boilerplate that an architecture model would not record. It only builds suggestion strings for later display, so it does not render a user interface itself.

Small helper that reads the reports directory on disk to check for existing markdown layer reports; used only by the upgrade command. It is a minor internal function that does filesystem reads, so it carries the data_persistence concern but has low architectural significance.

A small exported interface describing contextual metadata attached to errors (operation, related elements, partial progress). It is a minor supporting data shape in an error utility module with no callers. At most it would be modelled as a minor application data object.

A CLI options bag interface for the visualize command. It is a plain parameter type that only shapes command input and holds no architectural behaviour of its own. Its auth-related fields (noAuth, token) are configuration, not authentication logic, so no concerns are marked.

An exported TypeScript interface that defines the shape of a classified relationship record used by report generation. It carries classification, semantic and cross-layer analysis fields. As a domain record shape it fits data-model objectschema. It is a notable but internal type, so significance is 2.

A trivial getter that returns the codebasePath field from a module-level global options object. It has no logic and no cross-cutting behaviour, and it sits below the level an architecture model would record, even though Model.init and Model.load call it.

A trivial formatting wrapper that applies ANSI red coloring to a string when colors are enabled. It is a pure string formatter with no callers, below the level an architecture model would record. It only styles text and does not itself render or drive a user interface.

A validator class that checks cross-layer element references in an architecture model, including qualified references, layer hierarchy and manifest declarations. It is internal behaviour composed by the main Validator, so it is a notable application function rather than a standalone service. It does no I/O itself.

Utility module implementing file-based exclusive locking with stale-lock cleanup to protect changeset read-modify-write operations. It is internal infrastructure-like behaviour that a maintainer would name when explaining concurrency, and it directly creates and removes lock directories on disk, so it implements data persistence.

A small options interface for a CLI command (list, delete, or clear audit snapshots). It is a parameter shape that only matters to its command file, not a domain entity or contract. It is an implementation detail, so it is not modelled as an architecture element.

Interface defining the shape of a virtual projection of the architecture model (manifest, layers, relationships) with staged changes applied. It is an in-memory data structure used by the projection logic: a notable internal data object, not a canonical schema. It has no behaviour and performs no persistence itself.

Pure in-memory analysis function that detects exact and semantic duplicate relationships in a model for the audit orchestrator. It is internal automated behaviour, a notable unit of the model audit module. It does no I/O, auth, or UI work.

Trivial one-line delegation accessor on Model that forwards to GraphModel.getAllEdges, with no callers and no logic of its own. It is an implementation detail of the Model class rather than an architectural element, so it gets no layer.

Module providing a ChatLogger component that persists chat session messages and commands to per-session log files on disk. It is a reusable application utility component with logging (observability) and file persistence concerns, rather than a telemetry framework element. It is a notable internal unit within the chat subsystem.

A trivial one-line helper that clears an in-memory model cache. Its only caller is a unit test, so it is test-support plumbing. It touches no durable storage and is an implementation detail below the level an architecture model would record.

A private helper inside StatsCollector. It computes the set of elements that take part in no relationship, working over the in-memory model. It is a minor internal analysis step used only by collect(). It does no direct I/O; layer loading goes through the model.

Registers the MCP resource surface (spec manifests, layer schemas, model manifest, annotations) on an MCP server, making it the access point external MCP clients use. Its handlers read bundled schemas, the model and the annotation store from disk. It is an integration boundary but not an HTTP/OpenAPI route, so it is modelled as an application interface.

Core component that loads relationship predicates and per-layer relationship schemas from bundled JSON files and exposes a catalog of relationship types. It is used by commands, reports and audit orchestrators, which makes it a central shared component. It reads its definitions from files on disk.

A trivial ANSI color-formatting getter that wraps a string in bold green when colors are enabled. It is a formatting helper with no architectural meaning. It only styles terminal text and does not itself drive a user interface.

A small options interface configuring the staging-area commit operation (force, validate, dryRun). It is a passive parameter shape that matters only within the staging-area module, so it is a minor application data object rather than a canonical data-model entity.

A factory that builds the MCP server instance, registers its tool and resource surfaces, and warms the model cache. It assembles the MCP integration boundary, so it is significant, but it is internal composition behaviour rather than a contract. It writes only a single stderr warning, and model loading is delegated to loadModel.

A small utility module containing a single lookup helper that scans model layers to find an element's layer. It is shared helper code rather than an architecturally meaningful component. Layer loading may touch disk, but that happens inside Model, not in this module.

Trivial helper returning a constant list of heuristic name strings used by CbmAnalyzer. It contains no logic or behaviour of its own and is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element. It touches none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Small input-validation guard that rejects path traversal characters before the analyzer name is used to build a state directory path. Its only caller is getStateDir in the same file. It acts as a minor countermeasure against path traversal rather than a general helper. It does not itself touch storage.

GapAnalyzer is a domain analysis class used by AuditOrchestrator. It compares layer relationship templates against existing relationships to find missing ones and scores their priority and impact. It is a notable internal component of the audit subsystem. It does no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Small wrapper within the upgrade command that runs an integration update callback, wrapping it in a telemetry span and printing CLI progress and error messages. It is an internal helper used only by handleUpgrade, so its significance is minor. It instruments spans (observability) and writes console output (user_interface).

A small structural type describing the shape of a compiled spec bundle: version, schemas and predicates. It is a data-shape definition used internally by the spec loader. It has no callers and implements no behaviour, so it is a minor data-model object schema.

Module containing the unified Validator that orchestrates the five-stage model validation pipeline (schema, naming, reference, semantic, relationship). It is a central application component and creates tracing spans directly, so observability is true. Other concerns are delegated to the stage validators.

A one-line delegating wrapper that forwards the filter to SpecDataLoader.findRelationshipTypes. It has no logic of its own and no callers. The meaningful element is the SpecDataService class, not this pass-through method.

A one-line delegating wrapper that forwards to GraphModel.getNodesByLayer. It has no callers and no logic of its own. It is an implementation detail of the Model facade rather than an architectural element.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of a parsed spec node schema (id, layer, type, attributes) used by the audit subsystem. It is a domain record/DTO shape, so it fits data-model objectschema. It is notable within the audit module but not a central system boundary.

The module provides the GraphML exporter, a pluggable implementation of the Exporter interface that serializes the model into GraphML XML for external tools. It is a notable component within the export subsystem. It opens and closes telemetry spans itself, so observability applies. It returns a string rather than writing to disk.

Exported tracing helper that wraps OpenTelemetry tracer.startActiveSpan with a no-op fallback. It is the manual-instrumentation entry point used across commands, the model loader, validators and server middleware, so it is a significant observability element in the APM layer.

In-memory collection managing cross-element relationships within the core Model, with add, delete and query operations plus dirty tracking for saves. It is a notable internal unit of the core model. It does not itself do file I/O; it only serializes to and from arrays, so data_persistence is false.

Orchestrates sequential per-layer AI evaluation: builds prompts, invokes the Claude runner through AuditAIRunner, parses responses and aggregates scores. It is a notable process within the AI audit evaluator. The external call is delegated to the runner. It writes progress messages to stderr, which counts as CLI output.

A trivial state-check accessor on GoldenCopyCacheManager that returns whether the in-memory golden model and root path are set. It has no callers and no callees and does no I/O, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

Dispatcher method within the ChangesetExporter component that auto-detects the format and routes string data to the YAML, JSON or patch parsers. It is internal application behaviour that does not touch storage directly, since file reading happens in importFromFile. A maintainer would name it when explaining the exporter.

A small exported type describing a repository reference (git remote URL and commit SHA) within the source-reference data shape. It is a schema-like DTO with two optional properties, so it fits data-model objectschema. It is a minor supporting type with no behaviour and no callers listed.

MCP tool module exposing model element deletion (with cascade/dry-run) to external MCP clients. It is an application service at the integration boundary, persisting deletions via MutationHandler. It is not an HTTP route, so it belongs to the application layer rather than api.

ClaudeCodeClient is a concrete chat-client adapter, a BaseChatClient subclass that spawns the external Claude CLI subprocess, streams its JSON events and manages sessions. It instruments its own work with telemetry spans and chat logging. As a pluggable integration component used by client detection and streaming paths, it is architecturally significant.

Private helper that shallow-copies a Layer and its elements for read-only projection. It is an implementation detail of VirtualProjectionEngine, has a single caller, and does no I/O or cross-cutting work, so it is not an architectural element in its own right.

Bootstraps the OpenTelemetry NodeSDK, building the resource, the batch span processor, the resilient OTLP trace and log exporters and the tracer. That makes it the central TracerProvider configuration entry point, invoked by both the server and CLI entry points. It reads the manifest file from disk and wires export to an external OTLP collector.

A trivial ANSI formatting wrapper that applies dim styling to a string when colors are enabled. It is a pure formatting helper with no architectural role, so it would not be modelled as an element in any layer.

ImportManager is a registry and facade over the format importers (ArchiMate, OpenAPI). It dispatches import requests into the model and is the import subsystem's central component, used by the import command. It performs no I/O itself, so none of the concerns apply.

GraphModel is the central in-memory graph abstraction (nodes, edges, indices) underpinning Model, Layer and RelationshipGraph. It is a core application component of the architecture-modelling tool, a central abstraction used across the system. It is purely in-memory and does not itself persist or integrate externally.

Private timeout helper that returns a promise rejecting after a delay. It is used only by invoke to race against the AI call. This is a trivial implementation detail with no architectural meaning of its own and no cross-cutting concern.

Core export method of the MarkdownExporter that renders an architecture model into a Markdown document string. It is internal application behaviour implementing an exporter contract and is instrumented with telemetry spans. It returns a string and writes no files, so it does not persist data. It is notable within the export module but not a system boundary.

Trivial one-line delegation from SpecDataService to the loader's getStatistics, with no callers and no logic of its own. It is an implementation detail of the service facade, not an architecturally meaningful element in its own right.

File-backed persistence store for staged changesets (metadata.yaml/changes.yaml under documentation-robotics/changesets). Widely used by the staging area, validator, exporter, server and commands, so it is a central storage component. It is modelled as a data-store collection of changeset records.

This is a small CLI subcommand helper that checks a snapshot exists, deletes it through SnapshotStorage and prints a confirmation. It delegates persistence to the storage class, so only the console output counts as a concern. It is a minor internal function used by auditSnapshotsCommand.

Small internal method on MutationHandler that snapshots an element's JSON into before/after context fields. It has no callers and is a trivial state-capture helper, an implementation detail rather than an architectural element. It performs no persistence, I/O or telemetry itself.

A plain options interface for the CLI delete command, carrying flags such as force, cascade and dryRun. It is a minor data shape used only by its own command file and implements no cross-cutting concern itself, so it is modelled as a low-significance application data object.

Pure analysis module in the audit subsystem that detects semantically overlapping node types using Levenshtein and Jaccard similarity. It is internal automated behaviour with no I/O. It is a notable unit a maintainer would name when explaining the audit analysis pipeline, but it is not a system boundary.

Element is the central domain entity of the architecture model, aligned with spec-node.schema.json. It defines the required and optional fields, relationships and serialization to and from spec-node format. It has 71 callers across the codebase, making it a core data-model abstraction. It does not itself perform storage.

Registers the full DR model tool surface onto an MCP server and wraps each handler in a telemetry span. It defines the MCP access point through which external agents reach application services, so it is an application interface at a system boundary. It serves an external protocol and implements its own tracing.

Private helper that serializes a layer review to a JSON file in the output directory. It performs file persistence but is an implementation detail of AIEvaluator, not an architecturally meaningful element in its own right.

A small query method on DependencyTracker that returns the transitive descendants of an element in the dependency graph. It is internal application behaviour with no callers and no cross-cutting concerns, so it ranks as a minor internal unit.

A trivial state-setter on the Changeset class. It sets the status to 'staged' and updates the modified timestamp. This is an in-memory implementation detail of a data object with no persistence or other cross-cutting work, so it is not modelled as an element on its own.

A small type definition for the JSON-RPC notification message shape, used by the stdio client protocol. It is a protocol DTO schema with no behaviour of its own. It matters only locally within the stdio client, so its significance is minor.

Internal analyzer that scores the definition quality of a node schema (description and attribute documentation) for the audit orchestrator. It is pure in-memory analysis behavior used internally, so it fits best as an application function of notable but not core significance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Private method of ClaudeCodeAgent that monitors a spawned Claude Code subprocess, buffering stdout lines, parsing them into chat events, capturing stderr, and resolving a result on close or error. It is internal behaviour of the agent adapter that handles external process I/O, making it a notable application function.

An MCP tool module that exposes a model_reload operation to external MCP clients. It forces a fresh read of the model from disk and returns a summary. It is one of many tool definitions, so it is a notable service-level unit rather than a core boundary.

Shared result container used across all validators to accumulate errors and warnings, merge results and serialize them. It is an in-memory data object for automated processing and is widely used within the validation subsystem, but it is not a service or contract boundary itself.

Module defining CoverageAnalyzer, which computes relationship coverage metrics (isolation, predicate utilization, density) per layer for the audit subsystem. This is internal analytic behaviour within the audit component, so it fits an application function. It is a notable unit within the audit feature, but not a system boundary. Its console warnings are incidental.

Validator component that loads bundled relationship schemas from disk (manifest and per-layer JSON files) and validates model relationships, including cardinality, inside OTel spans. It is a pluggable part of the main Validator pipeline, so it is an application component. It reads files and emits telemetry spans itself.

Small pure helper that rates the confidence of a semantic match between two relationship types by comparing their category, transitivity and symmetry. Its only caller is detectModelDuplicates. It is an implementation detail of the duplicate-detection audit, not an element worth modelling on its own.

The module defines ExportManager, a registry and dispatcher that routes model exports to format-specific exporters and validates layer support. It is a central application component for the export subsystem. It does no I/O itself; it returns strings and delegates the work to the exporters.

A CLI command entry point that orchestrates scanning, recovery and repair of attribute-collision damage in the model. It persists repaired layers and an optional JSON report to disk, and renders colored terminal output. It is a notable maintenance command rather than a core architectural component.

A singleton test-infrastructure manager that builds and caches a shared golden Model on disk (in the tmp cache dir) and clones it for tests. It is test fixture scaffolding rather than production application logic. It is a notable testing asset, but none of the listed testing element types fits it well. It persists to the filesystem.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of an audit result record for node definition quality: description quality, attribute documentation ratio, issues and score. It is a pure data shape (DTO) with no behaviour and no callers in the graph, so it is a minor data-model object schema within the audit module.

This module defines an MCP tool (changeset_show) that exposes changeset detail to external MCP clients. It is a single tool among many, so significance is moderate. It loads persisted changesets via StagingAreaManager and serves the external MCP protocol.

A small return-type interface for the golden-copy cache that bundles a cloned Model, its root path, a cleanup callback and clone timing stats. It is a passive application data structure of minor significance, with no direct cross-cutting behaviour of its own.

Exported result type of the migration registry's apply operation, a structured record of applied model-version migrations. It is a passive application data object, not a canonical domain schema. It is a minor supporting type with no callers recorded and does no storage or I/O itself.

A small error subclass that supplies a fixed message, an error category and suggestion hints for a missing model. It is used by several commands, but it is error-handling boilerplate rather than an architectural element, so it is not modelled.

The module defines the central read-safe tool permission allowlist for AI agents in default mode and validates it. It is a security policy governing what agents may do. It formats the allowlist for the Claude Code and Copilot CLI flags and imports spawnSync, which suggests it probes or invokes external CLIs.

SpecDataService is a core service facade over SpecDataLoader that exposes query operations for spec layers, node types and relationships, with in-memory metadata caching. It is accessed via a global singleton. It is the application-level service for spec metadata. Persistence is delegated to the loader, and the in-memory cache does not count as durable storage.

A small options interface configuring file-lock timeout, retry and stale-lock behaviour. It is a parameter shape for a utility, not an architecturally meaningful element on its own. It defines no persistence itself and has no callers, so it ranks only as a minor internal unit.

An exported TypeScript interface that defines the shape of relationship type metadata in the relationship registry: id, predicate, inverse predicate, category and applicable layers. It is a domain type shape, so it is modelled as an object schema. It is notable within the registry module but not a core boundary.

CLI command module implementing relationship subcommands (add/remove/list) over the architecture model, with schema-driven validation, staging, and model persistence. It is a significant user-facing command component; it emits telemetry logs, renders CLI output, and saves model changes to disk.

FarmManifest is a core domain data object representing a multi-project farm manifest (farm.yaml). It is loaded from and saved to YAML on disk, validates its contents, and manages project membership, so it acts as a persistent application data object central to farm functionality.

A TypeScript interface describing the result structure of a verify comparison, with buckets for matched, graph-only, model-only and ignored entries. It is an internal data shape passed between analyzer code, so it fits application dataobject. It is minor and has no callers, and it implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Core module providing an in-memory registry of relationship types and relationship instances with source, layer and predicate indexes. It is a notable internal component of the model engine, slated for consolidation into GraphModel. It has no callers, does not touch durable storage, and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A 500-line core class that aggregates model statistics, relationship classification, data-model insights and quality metrics into the report data used by the report command. It is a significant reporting component that caches its results in memory. It does no direct storage I/O; catalog loading is delegated to RelationshipCatalog.

A trivial pure helper that counts properties with non-empty descriptions. Its only caller is NodeDefinitionAnalyzer.analyze. It does no I/O and implements no cross-cutting concern, so it sits below the level an architecture model would record.

A minimal exported type for the audit module that represents a graph connected component as a readonly list of node IDs. It is a small data shape with no behaviour and no callers, so it is a minor data-model object schema.

A high-level service module that wraps SpecDataLoader and exposes a query API over specification metadata (layers, node types, relationships), with in-memory caching. As a facade service central to spec operations, it is an application service. The loader performs the actual loading, and the cache here is in-memory only, so it has no direct persistence concern.

Shared component that wraps Claude invocation for the audit AI evaluators, adding rate limiting, timeouts and circuit-breaking on consecutive failures. It is the integration point to an external AI process, reused by both the node and relationship evaluators, so it is architecturally significant.

A small internal data-shape interface used only within the PlantUML exporter to hold element metadata for rendering. It is an implementation detail of the export module rather than a canonical domain entity or architectural element, so it is not modelled on its own.

A private helper that counts balance assessments by category and status for the markdown report. It is a trivial aggregation detail inside ReportGenerator, with no I/O and no cross-cutting behaviour, so it is not an architectural element on its own.

Registers the 'docs' CLI command group (generate, validate) with Commander, defining the user-facing CLI access point to documentation functionality. It is an application interface entry point wired from src.cli. It drives the CLI surface through help text and options, while the actual work is delegated to the action handlers.

A small fallback helper that reads the version field from package.json in dev mode. It is an implementation detail of getCliVersion with no architectural role. Reading a bundled package.json via require is not durable storage access, and the console.error fallback message is not observability instrumentation.

A simple CLI options bag (yes, dryRun, force) for the upgrade command. It is a parameter type local to the command and has no behaviour. It is boilerplate below the level an architecture model would record.

An exported result-shape interface carrying per-category relationship statistics (count, percentage, predicates, average strength) produced by the relationship classifier. It is a minor internal data structure for analysis output, not a canonical domain schema, so it is best modelled as a low-significance application data object.

Simple TypeScript interface describing per-layer statistics (element and relationship counts) used in model report data. It is a passive data structure for report generation, a minor internal DTO within the reports module, so it is best modelled as an application data object of low significance.

Orchestrates the model relationship audit. It loads the project model and relationship catalog from disk, then coordinates the coverage, gap, duplicate, balance and connectivity analyzers into an AuditReport. It is the central component behind the audit command, so data_persistence is true for the model load.

Bundled base JSON Schema document defining the canonical SpecNode and SpecNodeRelationship shapes that every model element and relationship conforms to. It is a central data-model contract for the spec system, shared across all layers, so it is modelled as a root JSON Schema with significance 3.

The module defines the Changeset domain object and its Change and StagedChangesetData shapes, which carry the staging workflow for model changes. It is a central passive data structure that the application manipulates, so it is modelled as a significant application data object. The visible code holds data and computes stats but does no storage I/O itself.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the shape of the integration version manifest: CLI version, install timestamp, and per-component file hashes with modification flags. It is a record/schema shape, so it belongs in the data model as an object schema. It is notable but not central, and it has no behaviour of its own, so no concerns apply.

DriftReport is a small exported result type produced by the base snapshot manager to describe model drift (hashes, drift flag, affected layers/elements). It is a passive application data structure, not a canonical domain schema. It has no callers and matters mainly within this module.

CLI command module implementing the 'info' command. It loads the model manifest from disk, sets span attributes, and renders formatted console output. It is one user-facing CLI command among many, so it is a notable but not core unit.

A bundled JSON Schema document defining the node schemas for the testing layer in the Documentation Robotics spec. It is a canonical schema contract consumed by the tool's validator, not test code itself. It is best modelled as a data-model root JSON Schema and is architecturally significant as a layer specification contract.

Type-only module defining the Importer contract plus options and result DTOs for format-specific importers. It is an extension-point interface that a maintainer would name when explaining the import subsystem. It contains no behaviour, so it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A CLI command module implementing element deletion: it loads the model, traces dependents, renders warnings and confirmation prompts, and persists the mutation. Telemetry spans are emitted inline. It is one of many user-facing commands, so it is modelled as an application function of notable significance.

Small internal TypeScript type describing an OpenAPI tag shape used by the exporter's serialization. It is not an actual API tag in the system's API surface, just a helper type for output formatting, so it has no standalone architectural significance.

CLI command module implementing 'dr docs generate/validate'. It spawns a bun subprocess to generate docs, reads and writes files in spec and temp directories, and prints CLI output. It is a notable command component within the CLI application.

Public entry method of the NodeOverlapDetector audit analysis: groups node schemas by layer and compares every pair to produce semantic overlap candidates. This is internal automated behaviour within the audit component, notable for explaining the module. It is pure in-memory logic with no I/O.
