Internal behavior of the RelationshipGraph audit component: it builds an in-memory graph from model elements and relationships for ModelAuditOrchestrator. This is notable audit logic with no persistence, I/O or UI, so it fits an application function of moderate significance.

Core logic for the CLI discover command: enumerates registered analyzers, detects installation, loads mapping metadata and decides selection/session behavior. It is internal application behavior separated from the CLI handler. Detection and mapping loading happen in callees, and the console.error call is incidental, so no cross-cutting concern is directly implemented here.

A trivial CLI error subclass that only builds a message and suggestion strings for invalid JSON input. It is a boilerplate error type used by one command, an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

MCP tool module exposing model statistics to external MCP clients. It is a thin service wrapper around StatsCollector and is one of many tools. It loads the model from disk and serves an external protocol, so data persistence and external integration are both true.

A CLI subcommand entry point that lists the node types for a layer by querying the spec loader and printing formatted output. It is a user-facing command handler exposing application functionality, so it is modelled as an application service. It is a minor, read-only command, and the console rendering is its UI concern.

Utility that locates the farm workspace root by checking the DR_FARM_PATH env var or walking up directories for farm.yaml. It is shared by all farm commands and the Model, so it is a notable internal application function. It probes the filesystem for file existence, which counts as reading durable storage.

Protected path-resolution helper that picks the production or development integration source directory by checking whether each exists. It is an internal detail of BaseIntegrationManager. The existence checks only probe the filesystem and never read or write durable data, so no persistence concern applies.

A core in-memory GraphModel mutation operation. It removes a node, updates the layer and type indices, cascades deletion to the node's edges, and bumps the version counter. This is notable internal behaviour of a central component. It persists nothing to durable storage, since all the work happens in memory.

Trivial state-mutation setter on the Changeset class: it sets the status to 'committed' and refreshes the modified timestamp. It does no persistence itself and has no callers. This is an implementation detail of the Changeset data object, not an architectural element on its own.

CLI subcommand handler that explicitly stages a model element into the active changeset. It orchestrates model loading and the StagingAreaManager, which performs the persistence. It sets span attributes and status directly and renders CLI/JSON output itself. This makes it a notable command-level application function, not a core component.

Registers all model tools on the MCP server, defining the exposed MCP tool surface and wrapping each handler in a telemetry span. It is a significant integration component at the MCP server boundary, and it directly implements span instrumentation and error status reporting.

A small query method on SpecDataService that derives the destination node types for a source from relationship specs already loaded in memory. It is internal application behaviour with no callers and no I/O. As a minor unit within the service, it is modelled as an application function of low significance.

Utility module that computes SHA256 file and directory hashes for change detection of integration files. It reads files from disk, which counts as data persistence. It is an internal helper supporting the integration install/update logic, so it is a minor application function.

An internal method of DependencyTracker that computes graph statistics (node, edge, cycle and connected-component counts) over the in-memory dependency graph. It has no callers and is a minor analytic function, not telemetry, so it is a minor application function with no cross-cutting concerns.

Exported TypeScript interface defining the record shape of an AI evaluation result for a spec node (alignment and documentation scores, reasoning, suggestions). It is a domain DTO in the audit subsystem, so it maps to a data-model object schema. It has moderate significance and no behavior or cross-cutting concerns.

Trivial setter that merges CLI options into a module-level global state object. It is a small configuration helper with no behaviour of its own, and it does not correspond to any architectural element type. It is used only by the CLI entry point and by tests.

MCP tool handler exposing model search to external MCP clients. It validates its arguments, loads the model through a shared helper, and filters elements by layer, type, query or source file. It is an externally exposed application service at the MCP boundary. Persistence is delegated to loadModel.

Simple accessor on RelationshipCatalog that builds category name/description records from loaded relationship types. It has no callers and is a minor query helper beneath the catalog component, so it is not a modelled element on its own. It performs no I/O itself; loading happens in ensureLoaded.

A trivial string-formatting helper that appends ' layer' to a formatted layer name. It is a pure formatting utility with no architectural role, so it should not be modelled as an element. It does not itself implement any cross-cutting concern.

CLIError is the shared error type, used by 63 callers across commands and MCP tools. It carries an exit code, suggestions and context, and formats coloured CLI output. It is a notable cross-cutting error contract, but not a service or component, so it is modelled as an application data object. The colourised terminal rendering counts as user-interface work.

A plain TypeScript interface that carries per-layer audit summary metrics (quality scores, issue counts) inside the node audit module. It is an internal result shape, best modelled as an application DataObject of minor significance. It performs no cross-cutting work, and nothing in the graph calls it.

A tiny local type describing the parsed shape of a manifest dist file, holding only a layers array of ids. It is used internally by the validator and has no callers or behaviour, so it is an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

Private helper that increments an in-memory cache-hit counter per changeset. It does lightweight internal metrics bookkeeping, not real telemetry infrastructure, and has no standalone architectural meaning. Observability is flagged because the symbol itself records the metric.

An in-memory registry class that indexes relationships and relationship-type metadata by source, layer and predicate, and validates predicates. It is a notable core component of the model engine, but only tests call it and it does no persistence or I/O, so it rates as a mid-significance application component.

Exported function in the analyzer session-state module. It reads the persisted status.json from disk, validates it, and returns null when the file is missing. This is internal file-backed state persistence for analyzers, a notable unit of that module but not a service boundary.

Small helper inside the conformance command that builds a per-layer map of element type names from the generated spec registry. It is a data-transformation utility with no behaviour of its own beyond reshaping registry output, so it is below the level an architecture model would record.

A small exported record type describing a model element that exists only in the architecture model, presumably from a drift or gap analysis. It is a plain DTO shape with no behavior, so it fits data-model objectschema. It is a minor result type inside the analyzer types file.
